recent_posts.title: Behind the Scenes Hardening Firefox with Claude Mythos Preview
recent_posts.summary: Mozilla shares a detailed behind-the-scenes account of how they used Claude Mythos Preview and other AI models to identify and fix 271 security bugs in Firefox. The team built an agentic harness on top of existing fuzzing infrastructure that can dynamically create and run reproducible test cases to confirm real bugs and dismiss false positives. Starting with Claude Opus 4.6, they parallelized jobs across ephemeral VMs targeting specific code areas. The pipeline covers the full security bug lifecycle: discovery, deduplication, triage, patching, and release. In total, 423 security bugs were fixed across April releases, including 180 sec-high, 80 sec-moderate, and 11 sec-low among the 271 Claude Mythos-identified bugs. Mozilla recommends other projects adopt similar agentic harnesses now, noting that simple initial prompts can be iterated into a scalable pipeline, and plans to integrate patch-based scanning into their CI system.

recent_posts.title: Trustworthy JavaScript for the Open Web
recent_posts.summary: Mozilla's Firefox Security Team introduces Web Application Integrity, Consistency and Transparency (WAICT), a new web platform proposal that cryptographically binds client-side JavaScript to a publicly auditable manifest. This addresses a fundamental trust gap in browser-based apps like encrypted messengers, where a malicious server could silently serve modified code. WAICT requires sites to opt in, after which browsers reject any unlogged code, making attacks observable and attributable. An early prototype is available in Firefox Nightly, developed in collaboration with Cloudflare, Freedom of the Press Foundation, and Meta. Specifications are being developed openly and early feedback is welcome.

recent_posts.title: Firefox Developer Edition and Beta: Try out Mozilla’s .rpm package!
recent_posts.summary: Mozilla has expanded its RPM package availability to Firefox Beta and Developer Edition on Linux. Previously only available for Nightly builds, the official Mozilla RPM repository now supports Firefox Beta, offering benefits like compiler-based performance optimizations, faster updates integrated into the release process, hardened security binaries, and automatic .desktop file creation. Setup instructions are provided for Fedora/dnf5, openSUSE/zypper, and other RPM-based distributions like RHEL, CentOS, and Rocky Linux. Language packs are also supported and can be installed automatically or manually.

recent_posts.title: Making WebAssembly a first-class language on the Web
recent_posts.summary: WebAssembly remains a second-class citizen on the web because it lacks direct integration with the web platform, requiring JavaScript glue code to access Web APIs and a cumbersome loading process. This creates a steep learning curve, language-specific toolchain complexity, performance overhead (measured at ~45% slower DOM operations), and forces developers to understand JavaScript even when using other languages. The WebAssembly Component Model is proposed as the solution: a standardized, self-contained executable format that multiple languages can target, supports direct Web API access without JS glue, and enables cross-language interoperability. Mozilla is actively implementing ESM integration for Wasm and working with the WebAssembly CG on the Component Model, with Google also evaluating it.

recent_posts.title: Goodbye innerHTML, Hello setHTML: Stronger XSS Protection in Firefox 148
recent_posts.summary: Firefox 148 is the first browser to ship the standardized Sanitizer API, which provides built-in XSS protection by sanitizing untrusted HTML before DOM insertion. The new `setHTML()` method replaces the error-prone `innerHTML` assignment, stripping dangerous elements and attributes by default. Developers can customize the sanitization configuration for stricter or more permissive rules, and can combine `setHTML()` with Trusted Types for centralized control over HTML injection. This approach requires minimal code changes and no dedicated security team, making XSS prevention accessible to a broader range of developers.

recent_posts.title: Launching Interop 2026
recent_posts.summary: Interop 2026 is a cross-browser initiative by Apple, Google, Igalia, Microsoft, and Mozilla to improve web compatibility. After Interop 2025 raised the overall score from 25 to 95 and brought features like View Transitions and CSS Anchor Positioning cross-browser, the 2026 focus includes 20 areas: new features like cross-document View Transitions, scroll-driven animations, WebTransport, CSS container style queries, and scoped custom element registries, plus reliability improvements for existing features like CSS scroll snap, WebRTC, and the Navigation API. Four investigation areas cover accessibility testing, mobile testing, JPEG XL, and WebVTT.

recent_posts.title: CRLite: Fast, private, and comprehensive certificate revocation checking in Firefox
recent_posts.summary: Firefox has deployed CRLite, a revolutionary certificate revocation checking system that provides comprehensive coverage of all revoked certificates while maintaining user privacy. Unlike traditional OCSP methods that leak browsing activity, CRLite downloads compact encodings of revocation data locally, updating every 12 hours. The system uses advanced Clubcard data structures with Ribbon filters, achieving 1000x better bandwidth efficiency than traditional Certificate Revocation Lists while covering 100% of revocations compared to Chrome's 1% coverage. Firefox will disable OCSP for domain-validated certificates in version 142, eliminating privacy leaks and improving TLS handshake performance by removing 100ms delays.

recent_posts.title: Improving Firefox Stability in the Enterprise by Reducing DLL Injection
recent_posts.summary: Starting with version 138, Firefox will include an alternative to DLL injection for Data Loss Prevention (DLP) deployments in enterprise environments. This change aims to improve browser stability by reducing the injection of third-party code, which often leads to crashes and unpredictable behavior. The implementation leverages the Content Analysis SDK, allowing Firefox to interact with DLP software more reliably and transparently.

recent_posts.title: Launching Interop 2025
recent_posts.summary: The Interop Project, a collaboration between browser vendors, aims to improve interoperability across the web platform. Building on the successes of Interop 2024, which saw a significant increase in the Interop score, Interop 2025 introduces 19 focus areas including storage access, WebRTC, and the removal of mutation events. The initiative also includes long-term investigations into mobile testing and accessibility features to further enhance the web's consistency across devices.

recent_posts.title: Introducing Uniffi for React Native: Rust-Powered Turbo Modules
recent_posts.summary: Mozilla and Filament have introduced Uniffi for React Native, a tool that allows developers to leverage the safety and performance benefits of Rust in cross-platform React Native apps. This tool helps offload heavy tasks to Rust, improving app performance and simplifying development. With this early release, developers can explore integrating Rust with React Native to create faster and more efficient apps.
